record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: For distributed differential privacy mechanisms that use discrete finite-support noise because Gaussian mechanisms are incompatible with secure shuffling or secure aggregation implementations, how can privacy accounting be tailored to those discrete noise distributions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a distributed differential privacy setting in which $n$ parties each hold a private vector and wish to compute an aggregate (for instance, a sum) under $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-differential privacy. Because the aggregation is performed through a cryptographic primitive — either a secure aggregation protocol that operates in a finite group $\mathbb{Z}_q^d$ with modular arithmetic, or a secure shuffler that permutes finitely encoded messages — the continuous Gaussian mechanism cannot be used: noise must be drawn from a distribution with discrete (and in practice finite) support so it is compatible with the underlying finite-precision, modular, or message-based protocol. Examples of such noises include the discrete Gaussian, discrete Laplace (two-sided geometric), Skellam, Pólya, and binomial distributions, possibly summed across the $n$ parties after local sampling.

Develop a rigorous privacy accounting framework for mechanisms of this form. Specifically, for a mechanism $M(x) = \big(\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i + Z_i)\big) \bmod q$ (or the shuffled analogue), where each $Z_i$ is sampled from a prescribed discrete, finite-support distribution $\mathcal{D}$, determine:

1. Tight $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-DP and Rényi-DP bounds for $M$ as a function of $n$, $q$, the per-party sensitivity, the parameters of $\mathcal{D}$, and the fraction of colluding parties.
2. Composition theorems for repeated applications of $M$ (e.g., across training rounds) that account for the discrete nature of $\mathcal{D}$ and any data quantization or modular wrap-around effects, and that match the tightness of continuous Gaussian accountants in the appropriate regime.
3. Privacy amplification results combining $\mathcal{D}$ with subsampling and/or secure shuffling.

Provide accountants whose bounds are tight (not merely obtained by approximating $\mathcal{D}$ by a continuous Gaussian or Laplace) and that remain computable for the parameter ranges arising in large-scale distributed training.
artifact.status_search_result: Tailored privacy accounting for several discrete noise distributions has been developed, notably the distributed discrete Gaussian mechanism with Rényi-DP analysis accounting for modular summation and quantization (Kairouz et al., 2021), the Skellam mechanism, and follow-up work on securely sampling discrete Gaussian noise via MPC (CCS 2023) and benchmarks of secure sampling protocols (2024). These results address the original need for accountants tailored to discrete finite-support noises compatible with secure aggregation/shuffling, but the broader program — tight accountants for arbitrary discrete distributions, full composition with subsampling and shuffling, and matching central-Gaussian tightness across all regimes — remains an active area of research, so the problem is best characterized as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: The Distributed Discrete Gaussian Mechanism for Federated Learning with Secure Aggregation
status_evidence.snippet: Privacy analysis for sums of discrete Gaussians accounting for effects of data quantization and modular summation arithmetic.
status_evidence.claim: Tailored accounting for discrete Gaussian noise under secure aggregation has been developed.

status_evidence.title: Securely Sampling Discrete Gaussian Noise for Multi-Party Differential Privacy (CCS 2023)
status_evidence.snippet: First MPC solution for sampling discrete Gaussian noise compatible with malicious secure MPC.
status_evidence.claim: Active follow-up addresses secure sampling of discrete DP noise, indicating ongoing progress.

status_evidence.title: Benchmarking Secure Sampling Protocols for Differential Privacy
status_evidence.snippet: Benchmarks of secure sampling protocols for DP noise distributions.
status_evidence.claim: The area remains an active research topic with multiple discrete-noise accountants being compared.
